title: Sorrify each named have of cases_hierarchical into a hole, keeping the exact glue
intent: Turn a Lean proof assembled from named `have` steps into the same skeleton with every `have` proof replaced by `:= by sorry`, so the declarations and the glue lines (`exact h2`, `exact h4`) survive intact and each `have` becomes a named hole a repair model can fill one at a time.

applicability.goal_shape: A Lean proof whose `by` block is a sequence of named `have` statements applied to close the goal, optionally under bullets and a `cases` split — the shape the function rewrites one `have` at a time by matching `have ` at a word boundary and parsing the declaration with `_parse_have_statement`.
applicability.use_when: you want to keep a proof's skeleton — every `have` declaration and the exact `exact hN` glue lines — while turning each `have` proof into a `sorry` hole, so the structure compiles as a sketch and a downstream model fills one hole at a time.
applicability.avoid_when: the block has no named `have` statements (nothing is rewritten), or a `have` cannot be parsed (`_parse_have_statement` returns no declaration, so that line is left as-is), or you need the proofs themselves rather than holes. The function only sordifies; it never checks that the original proofs were correct or that the holes are fillable.

claims.claim: The function's docstring states the move it performs: 'Replace the proofs of have statements with sorry while preserving the theorem structure.'

The same move runs in the harness: `HILBERTWorker` calls `replace_have_proofs_with_sorry(proof_sketch)` (line 1660) and verifies the result with `is_sorry_ok=True` (line 1672), so a model can repair the sorrified holes one at a time.

metrics.how_counted: the four have declarations on lines 180, 181, 185 and 187 are each rewritten to `:= by sorry`; the two application lines `exact h2` (line 184) and `exact h4` (line 190) pass through unchanged

consequences: The move preserves the theorem's skeleton — every `have` declaration, the case split and the exact `exact hN` glue — while replacing each leaf proof with a named hole, so the sketch still parses and a bounded prover can fill one hole at a time. Obligations it creates: (i) declaration fidelity — the `have` name and type must be reproduced exactly by `_parse_have_statement` or the glue's `exact hN` no longer names the hole; (ii) coverage — every `have` that the glue cites must itself be sorrified, or the sketch will not compile with `is_sorry_ok=True`; (iii) fillability is left to the caller — sorrifying does not check that the original proofs were correct or that the holes are solvable. Failure modes visible in the code: a `have` whose proof is a single line and a `have` whose proof spans several lines are both flattened to `:= by sorry`, so any dependence between children (h2 on h1, h4 on h3) survives only through the glue, and a `have` the parser cannot read (`have_declaration` falsy) is silently left with its original proof instead of being sorrified.
